items.title: From Population Averages to Individual Realities: A Debate on Using Intensive Longitudinal Methods in Mental Health Nursing Research
items.abstract: Accessible Summary Originality This debate essay introduces intensive longitudinal methods (ILMs), including daily diary methods, experience sampling methodology, ecological momentary assessment, and ambulatory assessment to psychiatric‐mental health nurses. It contrasts ILMs with conventional cross‐sectional and retrospective designs by showing how frequent, repeated measurements in everyday environments can reveal how psychiatric symptoms fluctuate and interact with contextual factors in real time. Significance ILMs support patient‐centred care and recovery‐oriented mental health care by generating individual‐level data that reflect each person's unique symptom patterns, triggers, and trajectories rather than relying only on population averages. Findings from ILM studies can inform more tailored nursing assessments and interventions—for example, distinguishing whether a patient's mood is more affected by sleep, social contact, or daily stressors—and support shared decision‐making between nurses and patients. ILMs can be practically embedded into clinical practice through smartphones, web applications, and wearable devices, with emerging opportunities to combine these methods with artificial intelligence for enhanced monitoring, early risk detection and care planning. Rigour The essay draws upon foundational textbooks and recent peer‐reviewed studies of ILMs to ensure that its methodical overview is based in established and up‐to‐date evidence. It discusses key methodological considerations, such as participant burden, missing data management, identification of confounders, and the need for measures that are sensitive to within‐person change and provides practical guidance for psychiatric‐mental health nursing researchers planning to use ILMs.

items.title: From predictive AI to autonomous food bioprocessing: a critical review of real-time quality monitoring, energy optimization, digital twins, and intelligent process control
items.abstract: Food bioprocessing is transitioning from conventional automation towards intelligent, data-driven, and increasingly autonomous manufacturing. A substantial gap nevertheless remains between accurate process prediction and reliable autonomous control. This critical narrative review examines the convergence of real-time sensing, artificial intelligence (AI), energy and process optimisation, hybrid physics–AI modelling, digital twins, and intelligent closed-loop control in food bioprocess engineering, with explicit attention to what has been demonstrated experimentally, at pilot scale, or only in simulation versus what remains conceptual. A structured narrative review informed by SANRA principles was conducted using Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, IEEE Xplore, and Google Scholar, with literature published up to 17 August 2026 considered and supplemented by a second, targeted search cycle addressing process analytical technology, electronic sensing, convolutional-network quality evaluation, and digital-twin applications in thermal, baking, and cold-chain processes. Evidence was synthesised according to the technological progression from monitoring and prediction to optimisation, digital twins, intelligent control, and autonomy. The evidence indicates substantial advances in smart sensing, machine learning, multimodal quality assessment, and multi-objective optimisation, with demonstrated opportunities to improve product quality, energy efficiency, productivity, and resource utilisation. Nevertheless, most applications remain concentrated at monitoring, predictive-modelling, and offline-optimisation stages, while validated industrial closed-loop and self-learning systems remain comparatively limited, and quantitative sustainability and economic evidence specific to autonomous food bioprocessing remains scarce. Digital twins and hybrid physics–AI approaches provide an important bridge towards autonomy by integrating physical process knowledge, real-time data, prediction, optimisation, and feedback control. This review proposes a six-level Food Bioprocess Autonomy Framework (FBAF), progressing from manual processing to self-learning autonomous bioprocessing, and situates it explicitly against ISA-95, RAMI 4.0, and SAE J3016-derived autonomy scales, providing measurable per-level criteria and illustrative classification of published systems. Future progress requires robust external validation, uncertainty-aware decision-making, interoperable infrastructure, cybersecurity, fail-safe control, and simultaneous optimisation of quality, safety, energy, productivity, and environmental and economic performance. The framework provides a foundation for benchmarking technological maturity and guiding the development of safe, scalable, and resource-efficient autonomous food-processing systems.

items.title: From Regression Models to Machine Learning Methods: A Bibliometric Review on Stock Market Prediction
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Stock market predictability remains a central question in financial economics, positioned at the intersection of asset pricing theory, econometric forecasting, and artificial intelligence. Using bibliometric methods, this study maps the intellectual history of this field by analyzing 12,495 publications from the Web of Science (WoS) Core Collection between 1994 and 2024. The analysis reveals a methodological shift in the literature: a transition from testing linear hypotheses anchored in classical market efficiency to engineering high‐dimensional representations of market environments using computational methods. Validated through triangulation of document co‐citation networks and keyword burst dynamics, the results trace the field's evolution from foundational stochastic volatility and factor models to contemporary deep learning and natural language applications, a transition accelerated by exogenous macroeconomic shocks. Furthermore, the research frontier is driven by three dimensions: measuring latent state variables via multimodal data, modeling strategic market interactions through agent‐based simulations, and imposing theoretical discipline on complex predictive architectures. This review offers a framework for integrating artificial intelligence with financial economics to develop more adaptive and interpretable pricing models.

items.title: Future Investment Forecast for Autonomous Mobility: AI, EVs, and Smart Infrastructure Driving the Next Mobility Revolution
items.abstract: Autonomous mobility is emerging as a major transformation in transportation, supported by advances in artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), sensing technologies, connectivity, electric vehicles (EVs), edge computing, and high-level vehicle automation. The convergence of these technologies is creating investment opportunities across vehicle manufacturing, semiconductor development, software engineering, telecommunications, smart infrastructure, cybersecurity, logistics, and mobility services. The autonomous mobility ecosystem is expanding beyond vehicle automation toward integrated transportation systems involving intelligent roads, connected infrastructure, cloud platforms, autonomous logistics, robotaxis, and Mobility-as-a-Service (MaaS). DataIntelo's current autonomous mobility ecosystem assessment places the global ecosystem value at USD 67.3 billion in 2025, with a projected value of USD 310.9 billion by 2034, representing a reported CAGR of 18.5%. This market value is used in this study as contextual evidence of ecosystem expansion and is distinguished from the investment index developed by the author. This study evaluates future investment opportunities in autonomous mobility between 2025 and 2035 using a qualitative and analytical framework incorporating technology readiness, infrastructure development, regulatory support, consumer adoption, and investment risk. Academic literature, government publications, transportation reports, electric mobility studies, technology assessments, and industry research were considered to identify major investment drivers and barriers. An author-developed normalized Autonomous Mobility Investment Growth Index is introduced, with 2025 assigned a baseline value of 100. The index reaches 135 in 2027, 210 in 2030, 285 in 2033, and 350 in 2035. The 2035 value therefore represents a 250% increase over the 2025 baseline and a 3.5-fold index level, rather than USD 350 billion of investment. The study identifies AI and software, autonomous vehicle systems, smart infrastructure, semiconductor technologies, connectivity, cybersecurity, autonomous logistics, robotaxis, and MaaS as major future investment areas. The findings indicate a progressive transition from research and pilot programs toward commercial deployment and integrated autonomous transportation ecosystems. items.title: Future Trends of AI, Big Data and Digital Business Transformation
items.abstract: artficial intelligence (AI) and big data analytics have moved from specialised technical functions to the core of how organizations compete, create value and organise work. This concluding chapter looks ahead. It examines the technological, organizational, regulatory and societal trends that are likely to shape the next phase of AI- and data-driven business, and it considers what these trends imply for managers, employees, policymakers and researchers. The chapter begins by situating current developments within the historical evolution of business computing and analytics. It then analyses major technology trends, including generative AI and foundation models, agentic AI systems, edge and real-time analytics, modern data architectures such as the lakehouse and data mesh, privacy-enhancing technologies, digital twins, and longer-horizon developments such as quantum computing. The chapter next develops a framework for digital business transformation grounded in dynamic capabilities theory, and it examines the changing nature of work, including the balance between automation and augmentation and the emerging evidence on generative AI and productivity. Governance and responsibility are treated as central rather than peripheral themes, with discussion of explainability, fairness, sustainability and the evolving regulatory landscape, including the European Union Artificial Intelligence Act, the NIST AI Risk Management Framework and India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023. Special attention is given to India's digital public infrastructure and national AI initiatives as a distinctive context for transformation. The chapter proposes a phased roadmap for organizations, identifies the capabilities and skills that future managers will need, and outlines a research agenda. It closes with a synthesis of the themes developed throughout the book.

items.title: Fuzzing FPGA Synthesis and Simulation Tools via LLM-Generated Syntax-Valid HDL Codes
items.abstract: Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) synthesis and simulation tools, such as Vivado , Quartus , Yosys , and Icarus Verilog , are key components of Electronic Design Automation (EDA) toolchains, translating high-level Hardware Description Language (HDL) designs into low-level gate netlists. However, defects in these compilers can propagate into the synthesized netlists, leading to crashes and functionally incorrect or even insecure hardware implementations and posing significant security risks. Existing fuzz testing approaches face several challenges, including limited diversity in primitive-cell types and a lack of feedback-guided exploration. These issues restrict their ability to thoroughly exercise the compilers and expose deep-seated defects. To address these challenges, we propose PolyHDL, which leverages the prompting Large Language Models (LLMs) for generating valid HDL designs to detect compiler defects in FPGA synthesis and simulation tools. By leveraging prompt learning and integrating feedback-driven guidance from primitive-cell diversity, PolyHDL generates semantically valid HDL designs with diverse primitive-cell combinations, thereby addressing the aforementioned challenges. Furthermore, through equivalence check, PolyHDL effectively reveals potential compiler defects in FPGA synthesis and simulation tools. Experimental results demonstrate that PolyHDL successfully identified and reported 18 valid defects in widely used toolchains, including Vivado , Yosys , Icarus Verilog , and Quartus within one month, 17 of which were confirmed by the official technical support, and achieved a 13.1%–13.4% improvement in code coverage over the SOTA approaches.

items.title: Game Theory Research on the Development and Promotion of Artificial Intelligence Teaching Platform Based on Multi-Participant University-Enterprise Collaboration
items.abstract: With the deep integration of artificial intelligence and education, university-enterprise cooperation has become a key approach for the development and promotion of artificial intelligence (AI) teaching platforms. However, differences in the interests of various stakeholders lead to insufficient stability in cooperation. Therefore, based on evolutionary game theory, this study constructs a dynamic game model involving enterprises, universities, and teachers. By establishing a replicating dynamic equation, the equilibrium point is solved and its stability is analyzed. Numerical simulations are then used to explore the evolutionary mechanism of each stakeholder’s strategy and key influencing factors. The study finds that enterprise strategy selection is influenced by teacher feedback and university support; university decisions focus on long-term educational benefits; and teachers’ willingness to use the platform depends on the balance between learning costs and benefits. Simulation analysis shows that factors such as benefit structure, training costs, and financial rewards significantly affect the evolutionary trend. This research provides theoretical basis and practical insights for promoting industry-university collaboration and optimizing platform construction and promotion.

items.title: Gamification User Types in Professional Football: Implications for Personalized Training Systems
items.abstract: Gamification is increasingly used in digital systems to influence user engagement and behavior. Identifying user types is important for designing personalized gamified systems. This study aims to identify the gamification user types that characterize professional football players, examine whether these types differ according to dominant foot, highest league played, and playing position, and provide implications for the design of gamified training environments. A survey was conducted with 113 male professional football players in Türkiye recruited through convenience sampling. Data were collected using the Turkish version of the Gamification User Types Scale and analyzed using descriptive statistics and Kruskal–Wallis tests. The most common user type among professional football players is Achiever, and the least common is Disruptor. No statistically detectable differences were observed according to dominant foot, highest league played, and playing position. A conceptual framework is provided to guide the design of personalized gamified training environments for athletes.

items.title: Generalizable iris presentation attack detection based on vision-language model
items.abstract: Owing to its uniqueness, stability, and high accuracy, iris recognition has been widely applied in fields such as financial payments and public security. However, driven by continuous technological advancements, attackers increasingly forge iris features to bypass identity-verification systems. Iris presentation attack detection (IPAD) aims to distinguish bona fide iris samples from various attack iris images. Existing methods for IPAD fail to generalize or remain robust under complex environmental conditions and diverse attack techniques, thus rendering them unsuitable for practical applications. To address the limitations of existing IPAD methods, which rely solely on visual feature modeling and exhibit insufficient generalization in scenarios involving both physical and digital attacks, this paper proposes an IPAD method that integrates a text-driven attention mechanism with a vision foundation model, named text-guided attention for IPAD. This method fuses information from both visual and textual modalities by leveraging the rich semantic knowledge of pretrained language models to guide the separation of bona fide and attack iris samples in the representation space. The learning process of the model is explicitly constrained and guided by utilizing textual semantics as a form of weak supervision, thus resulting in more robust and discriminative iris feature representations. This architecture is designed to overcome the challenges of adapting generic vision-language models to the fine-grained domain of IPAD. To enhance the capability of the method to perceive iris features, a fine-grained visual-text alignment framework based on textual prompts is introduced. This enables precise matching between iris image features and semantic information, thereby directing the model’s attention to subtle, attack-relevant regions, such as texture irregularities and printing artifacts. Moreover, multiple learnable textual prompts are employed to avoid bias from a single description, and their mean prototype features serve as semantic anchors for alignment. Furthermore, the method employs text-conditioned constraints based on slot attention to decouple bona fide and spoof features in the latent space, thereby improving generalization across diverse attack types. Experimental results on the LivDet-Iris 2017 and LivDet-Iris 2023 competition datasets reveal the superior performance of the proposed method in evaluating both cross-dataset textured contact lens and physical–digital joint attacks, thus confirming its strong generalizability in open-world scenarios. Specifically, compared with the respective best-performing baseline methods in the two evaluation settings, the proposed method reduces the average classification error rate (ACER) by 1.27 percentage points in the cross-dataset textured contact lens attack evaluation and lowers the overall average classification error rates (ACER1 and ACER2) by 12.03 and 6.46 percentage points, respectively, in the challenging physical–digital joint attack setting. Beyond quantitative evaluations, qualitative experiments utilizing textual prompts demonstrate that the model effectively captures discriminative features specific to bona fide and attack irises, confirming that the integration of textual guidance offers a more generalizable understanding of IPAD. This study offers a high-performance solution for IPAD and pioneers a promising technical direction by effectively leveraging vision-language foundational models to significantly enhance the security and generalizability of biometric systems.

items.title: Generative AI and digital productivity: Transitions, institutional misalignment, and human role redefinition
items.abstract: Generative AI is widely framed as a productivity tool. This framing understates its significance: when a technology lowers the cost of a fundamental input to the point of abundance, it disrupts not only the tools of an activity but the evaluation systems and professional cultures built around prior cost structures. This paper argues that generative AI constitutes the third transition in digital productivity, following the internet's reduction of information access costs and open data movements that restructured information flows, and develops five contributions toward understanding its institutional consequences. First, a three-transition model characterizes each transition by the input it makes abundant; the current transition makes structured written output abundant on demand. Second, a digitalization prerequisite thesis identifies machine-readable data foundations as a readiness condition most organizations and many individuals have not yet met. Third, a collaborative intelligence framework maps human comparative advantage shifting toward framing, critical evaluation, and contextual judgment as AI absorbs generative work, revealing that institutional credit concentrates at the production stage precisely where AI advantage is now greatest. Fourth, five structural tensions are identified: productivity surplus distribution and automatable job persistence, educational assessment disruption, AI authorship ambiguity, the professional performance threshold, and epistemic risks from fully AI-mediated communication chains. Fifth, a three-part governance framework (disclose, originate, accountable) provides actionable minimum conditions for AI-collaborative knowledge work across institutions and jurisdictions.

items.title: Generative AI and Higher Education in Morocco, Instructional Innovation, Student Entrepreneurship, and New Governance Challenges
items.abstract: The integration of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) into higher education is profoundly transforming pedagogical practices, the teacher-student relationship, and university governance models. Capable of producing textual, visual, or multimedia content, GenAI fosters personalized learning, intelligent tutoring, and the co-creation of resources. It also stimulates students' entrepreneurial spirit and redefines the role of teachers towards personalized guidance. However, this shift raises major ethical issues: the digital divide, algorithmic bias, and technological dependence. Our study explores how the use of GenAI modifies pedagogical practices, promotes student entrepreneurship, and influences governance within Moroccan higher education. A quantitative survey conducted among students and teachers, analyzed using statistical methods, allowed for the testing of a conceptual model integrating pedagogical innovation, governance, and entrepreneurship. The results propose an operational model for a human-centered digital transformation, adapted to the Moroccan context.

items.title: Generative AI in Fashion E-Commerce Product Imagery: An Experimental Test of Image Origin and Transparency Labelling on Consumer Trust, Perceived Product Quality and Purchase Intention
items.abstract: Retailers are increasingly replacing photographic model shoots with synthetic product imagery generated by text-to-image systems, a deployment decision that couples substantial production savings with an unresolved question about consumer response and about the transparency obligations attached to synthetic content. This study examines how AI-generated and photographic product images are evaluated in fashion e-commerce and how a visible origin label affects that evaluation. A 2 (image origin: AI-generated vs. photograph) × 2 (labelling: absent vs. present) between-subjects online experiment was conducted with 150 participants. Consumer trust, perceived product quality and purchase intention were measured with established scales, and general attitude toward artificial intelligence was tested as a moderator. Without labelling, no statistically significant differences between the two image types emerged on any dependent variable. The visible label reduced perceived product quality significantly but modestly, while effects on trust and purchase intention, the image origin by label interaction and moderation were not statistically significant.

items.title: Generative AI influences on political attitudes and suffrage behavior: Democratic resilience as an analytical framework in the United States
items.abstract: The rapid diffusion of generative artificial intelligence (AI) has introduced new challenges to democratic governance by transforming political communication, voter engagement, and information dissemination. Despite growing concerns about deepfakes, synthetic media, and AI-enabled persuasion, scholars have paid limited attention to how these technologies collectively influence voter attitudes and electoral behavior in contemporary United States elections. This study investigates the impact of generative AI technologies, including Large Language Models (LLMs), Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), conversational bots, and synthetic media, on political persuasion and democratic resilience during the transition from the 2024 U.S. Presidential Election cycle to the 2026 Midterm Election cycle. Using a qualitative doctrinal and policy-analysis methodology supported by election-related case studies, regulatory documents, platform policies, and emerging empirical evidence on AI-generated political content, the study evaluates how AI reshapes electoral communication. The findings reveal three significant trends. First, generative AI has accelerated the shift from mass political broadcasting to hyper-personalized, data-driven persuasion that can tailor messages to individual psychological and behavioral profiles at unprecedented scale and low cost. Second, AI-generated misinformation, including deceptive robocalls, synthetic visual advertisements, and inaccurate voting-information outputs, increases information pollution and creates opportunities for voter suppression and electoral manipulation. Third, beyond direct deception, AI contributes to affective polarization and strengthens the “Liar’s Dividend,” enabling political actors to challenge the authenticity of legitimate information and thereby eroding public trust in democratic institutions. The study contributes to the emerging literature on AI governance by developing an integrated conceptual framework that links hyper-personalized persuasion, information disorder, and democratic resilience in electoral environments. The analysis demonstrates that the principal democratic risk of generative AI lies not solely in misinformation but in its capacity to undermine public trust structurally and shared epistemic foundations. To address these challenges while preserving First Amendment protections, the study proposes a multi-layered regulatory framework incorporating mandatory content provenance standards, targeted amendments to the Federal Election Campaign Act (FECA), enhanced transparency obligations for political AI content, and conditional platform accountability measures during critical election periods. The findings provide policy-relevant guidance for regulators, election authorities, technology platforms, and democratic institutions seeking to safeguard electoral integrity in the age of generative AI.

items.title: Generative AI Potentials and Limits in Translating Iraqi Dialect in Literature: An Evaluation of Accuracy in Azher Jirjees’s At Rest in the Cherry Orchard
items.abstract: Recent academic scrutiny has considered the usage of artificial intelligence (AI) tools in transforming literary texts and studies have largely shown that AI translation tools can generate accurate outputs for common vocabulary. However, their performance may vary when dealing with difficult expressions related to dialects, cultural distinctions, and context-dependent meanings. In literary translation from Arabic, maintaining high level of accuracy in translating cultural expressions is challenging for AI systems. The main aim of this paper is to evaluate the accuracy level of four AI translations (ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, DeepSeek, and Gemini) and one human translation of Iraqi dialect in a novel by the Iraqi writer Azher Jirjees’ At Rest in the Cherry Orchard which has been translated by Jonathan Wright into English. In the current study, the researcher will not only assess the level of accuracy of translation but also evaluate the similarities and differences between the human translation and AI translations of the Iraqi dialect to see which is more reliable in understanding it. The researcher adopted Nababan’s translation accuracy theory to analyse the data in terms of accurate, less accurate, and inaccurate renditions. The analysis revealed that the level of accuracy was equal in the human translation, DeepSeek, and Gemini at 67% and 16% inaccuracy, while Copilot and ChatGPT recorded the lowest level of accuracy respectively. Overall, all the AI tools recorded 60% accuracy, 25% less accuracy, and 15% inaccuracy.

items.title: Generative AI Use and Reading Comprehension: Associations with Metacognitive Experience in Higher Education—A Quasi-Experimental Study
items.abstract: (1) Background: The integration of generative artificial intelligence (AI) into academic reading raises the question of whether such tools improve genuine comprehension or merely alter readers’ perception of it. (2) Objective: This study examined the association between generative AI use and reading performance and cognitive experience among university students reading a conceptually dense regulatory text. (3) Method: In a quasi-experimental, post-test-only design, with a single cross-sectional measurement per participant, 531 students from two Spanish higher education institutions read a Spanish-language regulatory text and were assigned to six conditions combining two systems (Microsoft Copilot Chat and ChatGPT 4 and 4.5) with varying pedagogical mediation, from unassisted reading to guided use with prior training. Literal comprehension and conceptual interpretation scores were assessed alongside perceptual measures of interest, attention, perceived learning and explanatory confidence. (4) Results: Literal comprehension did not differ across conditions (F(5, 525) = 0.85, p = 0.518, η2 = 0.008), whereas conceptual interpretation did (F(5, 525) = 3.55, p = 0.004, η2 = 0.033), although no AI condition outperformed unassisted reading. The clearest effect emerged for explanatory confidence (F(5, 525) = 12.58, p < 0.001, η2 = 0.107), followed by attention (p < 0.001, η2 = 0.027). Prior AI training was associated with the lowest interpretation and confidence scores. (5) Conclusions: Generative AI use was associated with changes in the subjective experience of reading, particularly explanatory confidence, more consistently than in actual performance. The observed pattern suggests that how students interact with generative AI may warrant at least as much attention as mere tool availability, although the present design does not permit this effect to be isolated from institutional and phase-related confounders.

items.title: Generative artificial intelligence adoption and the future of the primary care profession: an online survey of UK general practitioners’ experiences and opinions
items.abstract: Objective Use of large language model-based systems in healthcare has expanded rapidly since late 2022. Building on previous national surveys, we examined current generative AI (GenAI) use among UK general practitioners (GPs) and how GPs conceptualise artificial intelligence (AI), its clinical role and implications for professional practice. Methods and analysis We analysed data from the 2026 wave of the Generative AI in UK General Practice (GPAI-UK) survey is an annual, convenience sample online survey of UK GPs administered via Doctors.net.uk within a scheduled monthly omnibus targeting approximately 1000 responses. The questionnaire retained core items on GenAI use and added items on conceptualisations of AI, anticipated effects on skills and meaningfulness of work, perceived patient responses, career advice and long-term professional expectations. Descriptive statistics were used to analyse responses. Results A total of 1004 GPs completed the online survey. Just over half reported using GenAI in clinical practice (52%, 522/1004), most commonly ChatGPT, Heidi Health and Microsoft Copilot. Among users, 70% (363/522) reported that GenAI had reduced their work burden. Nearly half conceptualised GenAI as a collaborative technology working alongside clinicians (46%, 462/1004), while around one-fifth viewed it as a simple tool (21%, 209/1004) and 1 in 10 as a potential competitor (10%, 103/1004). Most expected GenAI to play at least a moderate role in routine practice within 5 years (69%, 693/1004). Looking ahead 10 years, one-third expected GenAI to change which GP skills matter most (34%, 337/1004), and 16% (163/1004) anticipated replacement of some core skills, most often documentation (811/1004), knowledge recall (509/1004) and diagnostic reasoning (442/1004). Many GPs said they would continue to encourage a career in general practice in the context of developments in AI tools; almost half had reservations (48%, 478/1004), nearly, one-third were not able to advise either way (32%, 317/1004). Most expected GenAI to substantially reshape the GP role while leaving GPs central to care (59%, 590/1004). Conclusion In this survey, over half of UK GP respondents used GenAI and primarily viewed it as a collaborative technology. GPs anticipated reconfiguration of skills and roles rather than widespread professional displacement. Understanding clinicians’ conceptualisations alongside adoption patterns is important for workforce planning, training and regulation.

items.title: Generative artificial intelligence in jazz improvisation: an Actor-Network Theory perspective
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GAI) plays an increasingly significant role in the artistic creation process. In the domain of highly interactive human-machine composition, GAI is no longer a passive tool but exhibits a certain degree of agency. Based on Actor-Network Theory (ANT), a social science theoretical framework proposed by French sociologist Bruno Latour and other scholars, GAI can be viewed as a non-human subject endowed with the status of an actor. In jazz improvisation, a representative creative activity, the agency of GAI is manifested in the generation of its specific musical works, presenting a contrast to human creation. Furthermore, this process reveals the leading and constraining factors in the actions of GAI, as well as the potential pathways and mutual interactions of its future co-creative development with humans.

items.title: Generative-AI/LLM-Enabled E-Assessment in Higher Education: A Bibliometric Analysis of Research Trends, Collaboration Networks, and Thematic Evolution
items.abstract: This study conducts a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of research on generative-AI/LLM-enabled e-assessment in higher education, drawing on 243 peer-reviewed journal articles published between 2023 and 2026 and indexed in the Scopus database. Employing VOSviewer and Bibliometrix software tools, the analysis integrates performance metrics and science mapping techniques. The findings reveal rapid growth, with annual publications increasing from 4 in 2023 to 117 by July 2026 (H-index = 35; 3854 total citations). China leads scientific production (39 articles), while Assessment and Evaluation in Higher Education is the most prolific journal (14 articles). The most cited study addresses LLM-generated feedback effectiveness (494 citations). VOSviewer keyword co-occurrence analysis identifies four thematic clusters: (1) generative AI and feedback processes, (2) health-professions education and methodological designs, (3) AI in education and pedagogical systems, and (4) large language models and automated assessment. The co-authorship network reveals a dispersed collaboration structure with 28.0% international co-authorship. Thematic evolution analysis reveals a shift from foundational explorations of AI viability toward specialized applications in feedback literacy and self-regulated learning. Several research gaps are tentatively identified as hypotheses for future verification, including the underrepresentation of developing countries, limited attention to ethical dimensions, and a scarcity of longitudinal studies.

items.title: Genotoxicity of ionizing radiation in occupationally exposed individuals: comparison between oral and conjunctival mucosal cells
items.abstract: Abstract Objective To evaluate genotoxic effects associated with occupational exposure to ionizing radiation using the micronucleus test in exfoliated cells from the oral and conjunctival mucosa of healthcare workers. Methods This pilot cross-sectional study included 22 participants (11 exposed and 11 controls). Micronuclei were quantified in 1000 epithelial cells from the oral and conjunctival mucosa of each participant. Between-group comparisons were performed using Student’s t -test or the Mann–Whitney U test, with effect size estimation. Negative binomial regression models with a log link function were fitted to assess whether the association between occupational exposure and oral micronucleus frequency remained after adjustment for age, alcohol consumption, and comorbidities. Results Oral micronucleus frequency was markedly higher in the exposed group than in controls (67.64 ± 39.80 vs. 1.91 ± 2.81; U = 0; p < .001; r = − 1.00). Occupational exposure remained significantly associated with oral micronucleus frequency after adjustment for age ( β = 3.373, SE = 0.438, p < .001; IRR = 29.16, 95% CI [12.36, 68.83]) and after additional adjustment for social alcohol consumption and comorbidities ( β = 3.767, SE = 0.562, p < .001; IRR = 43.24, 95% CI [14.38, 130.06]). No significant between-group differences were observed for oral binucleated cells or conjunctival micronuclei. Conclusion Occupational exposure to ionizing radiation was associated with a substantially higher frequency of micronuclei in oral mucosal cells, even after adjustment for potential confounders. These findings support the use of the oral micronucleus test as a practical biomonitoring tool in occupational health surveillance. Larger prospective and multicenter studies integrating biological biomarkers with individual dosimetry are warranted to confirm these results and further explore the conjunctival mucosa as a complementary biomatrix.

items.title: Geo-algorithmic Power: The Decline of Liberal Institutionalism and the Artificial Intelligence Dominance
items.abstract: This paper argues that the militarization of artificial intelligence (AI) is driving a structural transformation of the international order, marking a transition from norm-based security governance (Liberal Institutionalism – LI) to a new paradigm of geo-algorithmic power (GAP). This paradigm defines the capacity of states to shape the strategic environment through cyber dominance and digital infrastructural control. The findings indicate that algorithmic superiority is supplanting institutional legitimacy, thereby accelerating systemic fragmentation. By developing an original theoretical model, the research formulates hypotheses and employs a comparative design—applied to the United States, China, and the European Union—to demonstrate that algorithmic superiority can lead to strategic destabilization. The conclusions address potential trajectories for Romania’s international relations in the context of NATO and EU strategies, highlighting the need to build a defensive technological sovereignty that transcends the resolution of the conflict in Ukraine. A case study based on a hypothetical national security scenario reinforces the conviction that algorithmic superiority can ultimately supersede institutional legitimacy. Furthermore, liberal institutions must evolve into centers of expertise where specialized personnel curate the solutions proposed by AI.

items.title: GUIDED BY INNOVATION: A PHENOMENOLOGICAL STUDY OF VIRTUAL ELEMENTARY TEACHERS’ PERCEPTIONS OF GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE INTEGRATION
items.abstract: The purpose of this qualitative phenomenological study was to explore the lived experiences of elementary virtual teachers who integrate generative artificial intelligence (GAI) tools in their pedagogical practices at a large elementary virtual school. Participants were purposively sampled because those in the specified virtual school program provided relevant, experience-based insights and allowed the researcher practical, feasible access (Creswell & Poth, 2018). The participant sample for this study consisted of virtual elementary teachers who taught students in kindergarten through fifth grade. The researcher conducted semi-structured interviews with 10 teachers. The researcher followed Creswell and Poth’s (2018) data analysis spiral to systematically analyze data and determine themes. Four themes emerged from significant participant statements: efficiency, preservation of the teacher role, instructional enhancement, and AI literacy. The themes suggest that elementary virtual teachers are consistently balancing the positive elements of efficiency and enhanced instructional quality with the adverse aspects of misinformation, privacy protection, ethical concerns, and misuse. The themes suggest that virtual elementary teachers view GAI as a dynamic tool; however, its value depends on thoughtful, informed, and human-centered application. Future research would build on the findings by expanding the participant population and focusing on early adopters and the longitudinal implications of GAI use.

items.title: Harmonizing Vietnamese traditional and western medicine: a digital health blueprint and the IMKE architectural framework
items.abstract: The concurrent use of traditional and Western medicine is a global healthcare reality. In countries like Vietnam, dual-paradigm clinical guidelines actively mandate integrated treatments for high-prevalence chronic diseases. However, safe integration at the point of care is severely hindered by data fragmentation, profound epistemological differences, and a critical “shadow pharmacovigilance” crisis regarding underreported herb-drug interactions (HDIs). This paper analyzes the state-of-the-art of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in integrative healthcare and proposes the Integrative Medicine Knowledge Engine (IMKE), a novel architectural blueprint designed to safely bridge Vietnamese traditional medicine (VTM) and Western biomedicine. Shifting from siloed technical models to a clinical-first perspective, the IMKE conceptualizes a three-stage digital health pipeline: (1) advanced medical text mining to digitize unstructured traditional practitioner notes; (2) an Integrative Knowledge Graph (IKG) that maps holistic VTM diagnostic patterns to Western pharmacological databases and ICD-10 standards; and (3) an AI-driven Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS) for proactive HDI safety monitoring. We illustrate this architectural data flow through three clinical scenarios—Essential Hypertension, Type 2 Diabetes, and Rheumatoid Arthritis. These scenarios demonstrate the system’s theoretical capacity to retrieve culturally appropriate treatments, identify cross-paradigm therapeutic synergies, and generate explainable, mechanistic safety alerts that augment physician judgment while mitigating clinical alert fatigue. Ultimately, the IMKE framework provides a scalable, culturally inclusive roadmap for digital health. By translating centuries of experiential medical wisdom into an interoperable, computationally safeguarded infrastructure, this blueprint sets the foundation for evidence-based integrative care, future retrospective clinical validation, and enhanced patient safety.

items.title: Harnessing ultra-broadband random laser for massively parallel physical random bit generation and optical decision making
items.abstract: The relentless growth of data-intensive computing and artificial intelligence demands physical random number generators with unprecedented speed and parallelism to accelerate reinforcement learning and other stochastic decision-making algorithms. Despite recent advances in microring resonators, chaotic laser arrays, Fabry–Pérot semiconductor lasers, and random fiber lasers, existing schemes still suffer from inherent trade-offs between channel count and output power. Here, we demonstrate a high-power, ultra-broadband, spectrotemporally uncorrelated multi-wavelength Brillouin random fiber laser for massively parallel physical random bit generation and optical decision making. A 100-nm broadband optical frequency comb, comprising over 441 lines with a 30-dB peak power roll-off, is obtained through the synergistic enhancement of cascaded stimulated Brillouin scattering and quasi-phase-matched four-wave mixing. Notably, dispersion-shifted fiber further enhances the four-wave mixing effect, increasing the number of spectral lines. Rayleigh scattering and randomly distributed feedback break the correlations between wavelength channels, enabling direct and parallel random bit extraction without complex post-processing. Random bit sequences from 45 representative wavelength channels were experimentally characterized and verified using the NIST SP 800-22 statistical test suite. Operating at a 40 GSa/s sampling rate, each channel achieves 160 Gbps, yielding a theoretical maximum rate of 70.56 Tbps (160 Gbps × 441) for spectral lines within the 30-dB peak power roll-off. Furthermore, the proposed system experimentally supports four simultaneously acquired channels, while its scalability to at least 256 multi-armed bandit optimization problems, a representative class of stateless reinforcement-learning tasks, is demonstrated through offline reconstruction from independently acquired channel traces, providing a scalable photonic platform for decision-making acceleration.

items.title: Healthcare professionals’ awareness of climate change and its association with eco-anxiety and environmental sensitivity: a cross-sectional study
items.abstract: Abstract Background Healthcare professionals play an essential role in addressing the health impacts of climate change. Understanding how their awareness of climate issues and eco-anxiety relate to environmental sensitivity is critical for strengthening their capacity to respond to climate-related risks. This study aimed to examine the relationship between healthcare workers’ climate change awareness, levels of eco-anxiety, and their environmental sensitivity. Methods A cross-sectional, correlational design was employed. The study included 460 healthcare professionals aged 18 years or older working in clinical settings. Data were gathered using a socio-demographic form, the Environmental Sensitivity Scale, the Global Climate Change Awareness Scale, and the Eco-Anxiety Scale. Analyses were conducted using SPSS 24.0, including descriptive statistics, Spearman correlation, and multiple linear regression. Results Healthcare professionals demonstrated moderate levels of climate change awareness and environmental sensitivity, while eco-anxiety levels were moderate. Regression analysis showed that awareness of global climate change, being a nurse, being aged 45 years or older, and membership in an environmental organization were significant predictors of environmental sensitivity, whereas the rumination sub-dimension of eco-anxiety showed only a marginal, non-significant association ( p =0.064). Conclusions The findings indicate that cognitive engagement with climate-related concerns, climate awareness, and certain demographic characteristics are associated with environmental sensitivity among healthcare professionals. Enhancing educational efforts, institutional support, and environmental policies may strengthen their capacity to address climate-related health risks and promote environmentally responsible practices in healthcare settings.

items.title: Heat stress and heatwave trends across Türkiye (1975–2024) using the Extended Heat Index
items.abstract: Heat stress is an increasingly important climate-related hazard in regions experiencing rapid warming and changing temperature–humidity interactions. This study examines heat stress and heatwave trends across Türkiye during 1975–2024 using ERA5 reanalysis data aggregated to the provincial scale. Heat stress was quantified using the Extended Heat Index (EHI), which integrates air temperature and relative humidity to represent physiologically meaningful thermal exposure. EHI-based heat stress events were defined as periods with EHI ≥ 27 °C lasting at least three consecutive days, representing sustained health-relevant thermal stress rather than local extremes. Trends were quantified using Sen's slope estimator and the Mann–Kendall test. Results show a pronounced and spatially coherent intensification of EHI-based heat stress across Türkiye. Heatwave days increased by 6.51 days/decade and season length by 7.28 days/decade. Events became more frequent(+0.24 events/decade), longer(+1.49 days/decade), and more intense(+0.28 EHI units/decade), while the heatwave season shifted toward earlier onset(−2.85 days/decade) and later cessation(+2.50 days/decade). Although relative humidity declined across much of Türkiye, dew-point temperature and actual vapour pressure generally increased, indicating that this decline did not reflect widespread atmospheric drying. Instead, rapid warming increased saturation vapour pressure and vapour-pressure deficit. Temperature remained the dominant upward influence on EHI, while regional humidity conditions modified the magnitude of thermal stress. Overall, warming and increasing atmospheric evaporative demand have substantially reshaped heat-stress conditions across Türkiye. By translating ERA5 reanalysis into province-level EHI indicators and warning categories, this study provides climate-service information that can support heat-health adaptation planning, early-warning systems, public health preparedness and decision-making. Practical implications This study shows how long-term climate information can be translated into practical indicators for heat-related climate services and public-health preparedness in Türkiye. Using ERA5 reanalysis, province-level Extended Heat Index (EHI) indicators, heatwave characteristics, and warning categories were developed to track changes in health-relevant thermal stress in a nationally consistent way. The results show that heatwaves have become more frequent, longer, and more intense, while the heatwave season has expanded through earlier onset and later cessation. These changes suggest that heat preparedness should increasingly be considered as a seasonal and long-term planning issue, rather than only as a short-term response to isolated summer extremes. Heat-health action plans and early-warning systems The province-level EHI indicators can support the development of Heat-Health Action Plans and heat early-warning systems by providing information on sustained thermal stress that reflects both temperature and humidity. Because EHI accounts for combined temperature–humidity conditions, it can complement temperature-only warning products and provide a broader representation of heat exposure. A common EHI framework also allows long-term changes to be compared consistently across provinces. This can help national and provincial authorities identify areas where heat stress is increasing most rapidly and where preparedness may need to be strengthened. However, the absolute EHI threshold used in this study is not intended to replace locally calibrated warning thresholds. Where local climate, health-outcome, acclimatization, and population-vulnerability data are available, these can be used alongside the national framework to refine operational warning systems. Preparedness across the expanding heat season A key operational finding is the expansion of the heatwave season. At the national level, season length increased by approximately 7.3 days per decade, with both earlier onset and later cessation. This suggests that preparedness activities may need to begin earlier and continue beyond the conventional peak-summer period. Public-health surveillance, risk communication, emergency preparedness, and health-service planning could therefore be guided not only by fixed seasonal calendars, but also by indicators of heatwave onset, persistence, and cessation. Province-level EHI trends may help identify where earlier activation of preparedness measures is warranted and where monitoring should continue later into the warm season. Regional differences are also important for planning. In parts of the Marmara and Western Black Sea regions, the main change was a shift from Safe to Caution conditions, indicating more frequent moderate heat stress. In Mediterranean provinces, including Adana, Mersin, Osmaniye, and Hatay, increases were more pronounced in higher EHI warning categories. These patterns suggest that preparedness priorities should reflect the type and intensity of heat-stress change observed in each region rather than relying on a single national response pattern. Planning and adaptation implications across sectors for climate governance The implications of increasing heat stress extend beyond the health sector. Occupational health, urban planning, emergency management, agriculture, transport, and other sectors involving outdoor or high-temperature exposure may also benefit from this information. Province-level data on declining Safe days, increasing higher-risk EHI categories, and seasonal expansion can support strategic prioritization within national adaptation planning and provincial climate-risk assessments. For occupational health, these indicators may help identify regions and periods in which outdoor workers are increasingly exposed to sustained heat stress. For urban planning, the results provide a broad climatic baseline that can help identify areas where more detailed local assessment is needed. In rapidly urbanizing locations, province-scale warming may interact with localized urban heat-island effects, potentially increasing heat exposure beyond that represented by regional-scale reanalysis. High-resolution observations and city-level validation are therefore important before specific neighbourhood-scale or urban-design interventions are considered. Persistently warm nights are another area requiring greater attention. Nighttime heat can prolong thermal exposure beyond daytime peaks and reduce opportunities for physiological recovery. Future climate-service development would therefore benefit from research on nighttime-specific and other sub-daily EHI metrics, particularly where these can be linked with local health, exposure, and vulnerability data. Such work could complement daytime-oriented indicators and provide a more complete basis for heat-health planning. The province-scale framework should therefore be viewed primarily as a tool for strategic screening and prioritization. It can indicate where heat stress is changing and where further local assessment is most needed, but it should not replace local meteorological observations, neighbourhood-scale exposure studies, or health-based vulnerability assessments. Climate service integration and risk communication The EHI-based products developed in this study can help strengthen links between climate information providers and public-health institutions. Potential users include the Turkish State Meteorological Service, the Ministry of Health, provincial and municipal authorities, emergency management agencies, occupational health institutions, and regional adaptation planners. For operational climate services, useful products may include province-level heatwave trends, changes in EHI warning categories, seasonal timing indicators, and maps showing where heat stress is increasing most rapidly. These products can make complex reanalysis data easier to use in routine planning, preparedness, and communication. Future systems could build on this framework by combining the long-term ERA5 baseline with near-real-time meteorological station observations. This would help represent local temperature and humidity conditions more accurately, particularly in complex terrain and densely urbanized areas. Linking these climate indicators with health-surveillance data could also support the future development of locally calibrated health-response thresholds and more targeted warning services. Effective communication is also essential for translating EHI-based information into practical public-health action. EHI warning categories can provide a consistent way to communicate combined temperature and humidity stress, but they should be accompanied by simple public-health guidance explaining what the categories mean and what protective actions may be appropriate. Used in this way, the EHI framework can complement existing meteorological warning systems and support more integrated, health-oriented climate services for Türkiye.

items.title: HELO-APR: Enhancing Low-Resource Program Repair through Cross-Lingual Knowledge Transfer
items.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) perform well on automatic program repair (APR) for high-resource programming languages (HRPLs), but their effectiveness drops sharply in low-resource programming languages (LRPLs) due to the lack of sufficient verified buggy–fixed pairs for APR training. To address this challenge, we propose HELO-APR ( H igh-resource E nabled LO w-resource APR), a two-stage APR framework that enables cross-lingual transfer of repair knowledge from HRPLs to LRPLs. HELO-APR (1) constructs high-quality LRPL training data by synthesizing LRPL buggy–fixed pairs from their HRPL counterparts, preserving defect-type consistency while ensuring that the synthesized code is idiomatic; and (2) adopts a curriculum learning strategy that progressively performs HRPL repair learning, cross-lingual repair alignment, and LRPL repair adaptation, thereby improving repair effectiveness in LRPLs. Using C++ as the source HRPL and Ruby and Rust as the target LRPLs, experiments on xCodeEval show that HELO-APR achieves the best macro-average Pass@k results and outperforms strong baselines in most settings. It increases Pass@1 from 31.17% to 48.65% on DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B and from 1.67% to 11.97% on CodeLlama-7B, while improving syntactic validity by raising the macro-average target compilation rate on CodeLlama from 49.77% to 91.98%. On Defects4Ruby, HELO-APR increases BLEU-4 from 61.20 to 66.79 and ROUGE-1 from 76.76 to 83.59 on CodeLlama-7B, indicating higher similarity to developer patches in real-world settings. Finally, we conduct ablation studies to assess the necessity of each core component. These results suggest that verified cross-lingual supervision provides a reusable approach for improving LLM-based repair in low-resource programming languages.

items.title: Heterogeneous multi-AUV cooperative area search with an LLM-assisted hierarchical planning framework
items.abstract: In heterogeneous multi-AUV cooperative area search, existing methods often decompose the task region before assigning sub-regions to individual AUVs. However, coverage costs associated with platform capability differences, time-energy coupling, and temporal coordination constraints are often insufficiently considered during region decomposition, which may lead to suboptimal partitions and capability-task mismatches. To better account for these factors, a Voronoi-based region parameterization method is developed to formulate region decomposition and task allocation as a continuous optimization problem under coupled constraints. An improved CMA-ES-based optimization method, incorporating weighted K-means initialization and cost-guided directional sampling, is proposed to solve the resulting non-convex and non-smooth black-box problem. Furthermore, motivated by advances in large language models (LLMs), this paper establishes an LLM-assisted hierarchical planning framework in which operators’ natural-language task intentions are mapped to the inputs and constraints of the optimization method, enabling flexible task-level planning and pre-deployment iterative plan refinement. Simulation results show that the proposed framework effectively balances task completion time, temporal coordination, and energy utilization, while supporting iterative refinement of plans prior to deployment. These results highlight the potential of integrating LLM-based task interpretation with optimization-based planning for cooperative underwater robotic systems.

items.title: HEY @GROK, IS THIS TRUE? AN EXAMINATION OF NEWS VERIFICATION PRACTICES ON X
items.abstract: AbstractGenerative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) systems have become a new actor in news verification practices. This study aims to examine the news verification requests that Turkish-speaking users on Platform X make to Grok, as well as Grok’s role in the news verification process. In the study, 276 news verification requests directed at Grok on the X platform during June 2026 were analyzed using qualitative content analysis. As part of the analysis, the verification requests were evaluated based on news topic, content type, news source, account verification status, account verification badge, whether the news was national or international, and Grok’s responses. The findings indicate that Grok can respond quickly to news verification requests and adapt to the user’s communication style, meticulously detailing the verification process. The news topics with the highest number of verification requests were, in order of sports, politics, and crime news, and explanatory content was verified more than other content types. It was also determined that the vast majority of accounts requesting news verification were anonymous, that verification requests covered both national and international news, and that users tended to trust Grok, as they requested verification from it regardless of whether the content was shared by an official organization. In the study, Grok is evaluated as an AI-based verification tool that supports the news verification ecosystem on the X platform, facilitates users’ information verification practices, and functions effectively through the Community Notes mechanism.Keywords: Large Language Models, Generative Artificial Intelligence, X, Grok.

items.title: How Implementation Context Shapes Clinician Acceptance and Engagement with Guideline-Based Clinical Decision Support Systems in Primary Care: A Qualitative Study
items.abstract: Background: Guideline-based clinical decision support (CDS) tools have become central to promoting evidence-based, high-quality primary care. Despite widespread implementation, clinician adoption and sustained use remain inconsistent. Existing research has typically examined technological usability or organizational implementation factors separately, providing limited understanding of how these influences interact in real-world primary care settings. This study examined how organizational implementation context and clinician technology acceptance jointly shape adoption and sustained use of guideline-based CDS tools in US primary care using an integrated Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) and Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) perspective. Methods: A qualitative study using reflexive thematic analysis was conducted with 13 US primary care clinicians, including physicians, nurse practitioners, physician assistants, and pharmacists with prescribing authority. Participants were purposively recruited from diverse ambulatory settings. Semi-structured interviews explored experiences with CDS usability, workflow integration, organizational support, trust, cognitive burden, and implementation processes. Data were analyzed iteratively using Braun and Clarke’s reflexive thematic analysis, informed by CFIR and TAM. Results: Six interrelated themes emerged. Clinician acceptance and sustained use of CDS were shaped by (1) workflow integration, (2) organizational legitimacy and leadership support, (3) preservation of clinical judgment, particularly with emerging AI-enabled CDS, (4) social reinforcement and team-based implementation, (5) cognitive and resource constraints, and (6) clinician role, experience, and digital comfort. Across themes, acceptance was driven less by technological capability than by the interaction of workflow design, organizational context, implementation climate, trust, and clinician perceptions. Conclusion: Guideline-based CDS implementation is fundamentally a sociotechnical process requiring alignment between technology, workflow, organizational context, and clinician acceptance. Integrating CFIR and TAM provides a comprehensive framework for understanding these interactions. The findings informed the TRUST framework, which offers practical implementation guidance emphasizing tailored workflow integration, reinforced organizational legitimacy, usability, social reinforcement, and transparent, trustworthy AI-supported CDS to support sustainable implementation in primary care. items.title: How Safe Is Your Screen? Understanding and Detecting Privacy Leaks in Sensitive Activities
items.abstract: Android apps handle sensitive data, often displayed on screens (i.e., Activities), and protecting these activities is vital for ensuring user privacy. Several studies have demonstrated the risk of private data leakage via screen capture and identified malware exploiting this vulnerability. To mitigate such threats, Google introduced FLAG_SECURE, an activity-level security feature that protects an Activity when set by blocking screen capture and restricting display on non-secure devices. Proper usage of this security feature could significantly reduce data leakage risks. However, to the best of our knowledge, its adoption across diverse Android apps has not been systematically studied. In this work, we present a large-scale empirical study of screenshot-based vulnerabilities in Android apps using a systematic static analysis pipeline, ASSA. The pipeline automatically constructs UI models of activities and fragments by leveraging a customized version of Frontmatter, and combines them with a Large Language Model (LLM) to infer runtime context and identify sensitive user data rendered on screens. We apply ASSA to 5,667 popular real-world Android apps and find that 19.8% contain at least one activity that displays sensitive information without screen-capture protection, while 87.2% of apps do not apply FLAG_SECURE to any activity, exposing credentials, financial information, and location data to screenshot attacks. Beyond quantifying prevalence, we analyze FLAG_SECURE usage patterns and establish a taxonomy that captures diverse factors influencing developers’ decisions to adopt or omit screen protection, including intentional privacy protection, intellectual property safeguarding, and unintentional inheritance from base activities. To assess real-world impact, we further conduct in-depth case studies on 200 vulnerable apps and responsibly disclose our findings to the affected vendors, receiving 6 confirmed patches and 20 acknowledgments, including 11 vendors who reported ongoing efforts toward mitigation. These findings indicate that screenshot-based vulnerabilities are not only widespread but also systematically overlooked in practice, highlighting the need for greater awareness and more careful handling of sensitive on-screen information by developers.

items.title: How well do large language models answer postoperative lumbar fusion questions? A blinded comparative analysis of accuracy, quality, readability, and safety-related content
items.abstract: Background Patients recovering from lumbar fusion increasingly seek guidance from large language model (LLM) chatbots when their surgeon is unavailable, but the accuracy, completeness, and safety-related content of such responses have not been compared across models for the postoperative period. Objective To compare the accuracy, quality, safety-related content, and readability of responses from ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude to frequently asked postoperative lumbar fusion questions, and to identify the question types for which responses are weakest. Methods Thirty questions, compiled by three neurosurgeons and grouped into six clinical categories, were submitted to each model, each with a standardized, patient-oriented prompt requesting warning signs. Ninety anonymized, randomized responses were rated independently by three blinded neurosurgeons for accuracy and four quality subdomains (clarity, completeness, relevance, and patient safety) on 4-point scales. Readability (Flesch–Kincaid, Flesch Reading Ease, and Gunning Fog), word count, and responses meeting an operational screening criterion for potential harm were also assessed. Models were compared with Friedman and Holm-corrected pairwise tests. Results Accuracy was high for all models without significant differences. Quality, clarity, completeness, relevance, and patient safety differed globally, but effect sizes were small (Kendall's W : 0.10–0.21) and, after correction across the six outcome families, only quality and completeness remained significant, with Gemini scoring lower than ChatGPT and Claude. Gemini had the most favorable readability. ChatGPT responses were the shortest (mean 294 vs. 462 and 445 words); length was unrelated to completeness or readability. Two Gemini responses (6.7%) and none from ChatGPT or Claude met a post hoc operational screening criterion for potential harm (a score of ≤2 on accuracy or patient safety from at least one of three raters, without concurrence from the other two); no response was adjudicated as actually harmful. In exploratory question- and category-level analyses, responses tended to be rated highest for standardized questions and lowest for those requiring individualized judgment or interpretation of wound-related symptoms. Conclusion Responses from contemporary LLMs to common postoperative lumbar fusion questions were generally rated as accurate, with small between-model differences and a model-level divergence between readability and completeness. Because safety-related content was explicitly prompted and no patient outcomes were assessed, these findings describe the quality of safety-related information rather than clinical safety. LLMs may support postoperative patient education but should not replace physician guidance, particularly for warning signs and patient-specific recovery decisions.

items.abstract: Background: Intensive computer use among administrative workers increases exposure to visual ergonomic factors that may contribute to Computer Vision Syndrome (CVS). Workplace illumination, duration of computer use, and length of employment are important factors to consider in preventing occupational visual complaints. Objective: This study aimed to analyze the association between illumination intensity, duration of computer use, length of employment, and CVS complaints among administrative workers at PT. X in Batam City. Methods: A quantitative study with a cross-sectional design was conducted among 31 administrative workers. Workplace illumination intensity was measured using a lux meter, while the duration of computer use and length of employment were obtained from respondent data. CVS complaints were assessed using the Computer Vision Syndrome Questionnaire (CVS-Q). Bivariate associations were analyzed using Fisher's exact test at a significance level of α=0.05. Results: A total of 77.4% of respondents worked under illumination levels below the occupational standard, 38.7% used computers continuously for ≥120 minutes, 61.3% had worked for ≥5 years, and 80.6% experienced CVS. All respondents exposed to illumination below the standard experienced CVS. A statistically significant association was found between workplace illumination and CVS complaints (p<0.001). In contrast, the duration of computer use (p=0.059) and length of employment (p=0.653) were not significantly associated with CVS complaints. Conclusion: Workplace illumination was significantly associated with CVS complaints among administrative workers, whereas the duration of computer use and length of employment showed no statistically significant associations. Improving workplace illumination according to applicable standards and implementing visual ergonomic measures are recommended to prevent CVS among computer-based workers.Keywords: Computer Vision Syndrome; visual ergonomics; illumination; screen time; length of employment

items.title: HUBUNGAN USIA, MASA KERJA, DAN KELUHAN LOW BACK PAIN PADA PEGAWAI PEMERINTAH KOTA BATAM
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Background: Low back pain (LBP) is one of the most common musculoskeletal disorders among office workers due to prolonged sitting, continuous computer use, and poor ergonomic posture. Age and length of employment are factors suspected to contribute to LBP complaints because they are associated with degenerative changes in the musculoskeletal system and cumulative exposure to occupational risk factors. Methods: This study employed an analytical observational design with a cross-sectional approach. The study population consisted of all employees of the Department of Culture and Tourism and the Department of Communication and Informatics of Batam City Government who met the study criteria. A total of 86 respondents were selected using proportionate stratified random sampling. Data were analyzed using the Chi-Square test with a significance level of p<0.05. Results: Statistical analysis showed a significant relationship between age and Low Back Pain complaints (p=0.019) and a significant relationship between length of employment and Low Back Pain complaints (p<0.001). Conclusion: There was a significant relationship between age and length of employment and Low back pain complaints among employees of the Department of Culture and Tourism and the Department of Communication and Informatics of Batam City Government Keywords: Age, Length of Employment, Low back pain.
